rulings.why: The page cannot tell these changes from the row: split:refrain.1.1: p513-strip800.jpg and p513-strip1600.jpg system 3, the refrain row: the word where the split opens a line is the pronoun I, printed with a capital wherever it stands. The header on p513-strip0.jpg (8.7.8.7.Ref) gives the refrain no syllable counts, so nothing shows that no line opens there. split:refrain.1.2: p513-strip1600.jpg system 3, the refrain row: the word where the split opens a line is a pronoun of God, which this page prints with a capital wherever it stands (mid-row in stanza 1's row on p513-strip0.jpg system 1 and twice in the refrain). The refrain has no syllable counts in the header. join:refrain.1.2: p513-strip1600.jpg, the end of system 3 and the start of system 4: line 3 opens on the name Jesus, printed with a capital wherever it stands, after line 2's closing exclamation mark. The header (8.7.8.7.Ref) gives the refrain no syllable counts, so nothing fixes the break. moveup:refrain.1.2: p513-strip1600.jpg system 4, the refrain row: the moved word and the word that would then open line 3 are both the name Jesus, each printed with a capital wherever it stands. The header (8.7.8.7.Ref) gives the refrain no syllable counts, so nothing shows where line 3 opens. join:refrain.1.3: p513-strip1600.jpg system 4, the refrain row: line 4 opens on the interjection O, printed with a capital wherever it stands, after line 3's closing exclamation mark. The header (8.7.8.7.Ref) gives the refrain no syllable counts, so nothing fixes the break. movedown:refrain.1.3: p513-strip1600.jpg system 4, the refrain row: the moved word is the name Jesus, printed with a capital wherever it stands, and the word it would push mid-line is the interjection O, also always a capital. The header (8.7.8.7.Ref) gives the refrain no syllable counts, so nothing fixes the break.
